item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft OneDrive: Updated placement of the Create or upload button in OneDrive for the web

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft Graph APIs for Copilot cost management
item.description:
[What and Why:]

Microsoft is introducing Microsoft Graph APIs for Copilot cost management, giving organizations a programmatic way to manage Copilot credit spending policies, monitor credit balances, and handle end-user requests for additional credits.

Administrators and developers can use the APIs to retrieve tenant, user, and per-service credit balances; create, update, and delete spending policies; assign security groups to policies; configure service-specific settings; and set up email threshold alerts. They can also retrieve, approve, or reject credit requests.

These APIs integrate Copilot cost management with existing administration and FinOps processes. This initial release, available through the Microsoft Graph beta surface, focuses on spending-policy administration and balance information; detailed consumption reporting is not included.

[Rollout Schedule:]

Public Preview (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out to the beta endpoint in mid-October 2026.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Who is affected:

  • Administrators and developers who manage Copilot credit spending policies via Microsoft Graph.

What will happen:

  • Organizations gain a new programmatic way to integrate Copilot credit cost management with existing administration and FinOps processes.
  • There is no change to the end-user experience, and no action is required for organizations that do not plan to use these APIs.
  • Detailed consumption reporting is not included in this release.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

No action is required if your organization does not plan to use these APIs. If you do plan to use them, we recommend you:

  • Review the Microsoft Graph documentation for available beta endpoints and current limitations.
  • Determine the Microsoft Graph permissions and authentication requirements for the operations you plan to automate.
  • Identify which existing administration or FinOps processes you want to integrate with Copilot cost management.
  • Determine which security groups should be assigned to Copilot spending policies, where applicable.
  • Review requirements for configuring credit threshold email alerts and alert recipients.

A General Availability date is not currently available.

[Compliance considerations:]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [planForChange] Microsoft Teams: Retirement of the Turn off IntelliFrame option for online participants
item.description:
[What and why]

We are retiring the ability for online participants to turn off IntelliFrame for their own view in meetings with a Microsoft Teams Room that has Cloud IntelliFrame enabled. This change provides all online participants with the same view of the room, as configured on the Teams Rooms device.

Currently, online participants using Microsoft Teams desktop on Windows and Mac can right-click the video tile of a Teams Room using Cloud IntelliFrame and select Turn off IntelliFrame. This switches to the standard room view only on their own Teams client.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Rollout will begin in late November 2026 and is expected to complete by early January 2027.
  • General Availability (GCC, GCC High): Rollout will begin in mid-December 2026 and is expected to complete by late January 2027.

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Online participants using Microsoft Teams desktop on Windows and Mac who join meetings with a Microsoft Teams Room using Cloud IntelliFrame.

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Teams for Windows
  • Microsoft Teams for Mac
  • Microsoft Teams Rooms using Cloud IntelliFrame

What will happen

  • The Turn off IntelliFrame option will be removed for online participants.
  • If Cloud IntelliFrame is enabled for the room, online participants will see the IntelliFrame view sent by the Teams Room. If Cloud IntelliFrame is not enabled for the room, online participants will see the standard room view.
  • This change does not affect how Cloud IntelliFrame is enabled or configured on Teams Rooms devices or any admin policies.
  • In-room participants can continue to turn off IntelliFrame from the room console settings.

[Action required and recommendations]

No admin action is required. We recommend that you notify users who join meetings with IntelliFrame-enabled rooms about this change and update internal documentation that references the Turn off IntelliFrame option.

[Learn more]

  • Cloud IntelliFrame - Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Learn

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft Teams: Streaming switchboard for NDI sources in meetings and events
item.description:

A new streaming switchboard in Microsoft Teams will allow event producers to more easily manage and send NDI® sources to production software during Teams meetings and events. Event producers can individually select and stream up to eight NDI sources directly from a Teams meeting or event.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning in early November 2026 and expected to complete by mid-November 2026

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Event producers who use NDI streaming in Microsoft Teams meetings and events

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Teams

What will happen

  • Event producers will be able to individually select and stream up to eight NDI sources from a Teams meeting or event.
  • To access the feature during a meeting or event, select More actions, then Streaming > Streaming switchboard.
  • Admins must enable NDI streaming before users can use the feature.
  • Users must turn on production capabilities in Teams before using NDI broadcast production. 

[Action required and recommendations]

To prepare:

  • Enable AllowNDIStreaming for the appropriate users through the CsTeamsMeetingPolicy cmdlet.
  • Instruct affected users to turn on production capabilities in Teams.

Learn more

  • Allow broadcast production in Teams meetings with NDI and SDI hardware - Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Learn

[Compliance considerations]

QuestionAnswer

Admins can control NDI® streaming through the AllowNDIStreaming setting in CsTeamsMeetingPolicy. The provided source does not specify whether the control can be managed through Entra ID group membership.
Does the change allow a user to enable and disable the feature themselves?Yes. After an admin enables NDI streaming, users must turn on production capabilities in Teams.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft Authenticator: Usability improvements for iOS and Android
item.description:
[What and why]

We’re updating Microsoft Authenticator with several usability improvements across iOS and Android. These updates include a refreshed home experience, clearer guidance for accounts that need to be restored, improvements to restoration and sign-in flows, and additional prompts designed to help keep Authenticator working reliably. Availability and timing vary by platform.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, and DoD): Beginning in October 2026 and expected to complete in November 2026
  • The improved restoration experience for push notifications and passwordless sign-in will be available on iOS first, with Android planned to follow in January 2027.

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Users of Microsoft Authenticator on iOS and Android

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Authenticator for iOS and Android

What will happen

  • Improved Authenticator home experience, iOS and Android: The Authenticator home page is being updated to improve the experience when users view and manage their accounts. On Android, this update will be available in November 2026.

iOs:

Android:

  • Clearer notification for accounts that haven’t been restored, iOS and Android: Users with accounts that have not yet been restored will see a banner informing them that those accounts require attention

. 

  • Improved first-run guidance for account restoration, iOS and Android: The first-run experience will more clearly show which accounts need to be restored, giving users additional context during Authenticator setup.

  • App rating prompt during sign-in, iOS only: Users may see an option to rate Microsoft Authenticator as part of the sign-in experience, giving them an opportunity to provide feedback about the app. 
  • Improved restoration experience for push notifications and passwordless sign-in: The restoration flow is being improved for users who use push notifications and passwordless sign-in. This improvement will be available on iOS first, with Android planned for January 2027. 
  • Prompt to exclude Authenticator from battery optimization, Android only: After successfully completing an interactive authentication, users may see a non-blocking prompt to exclude Authenticator from Android battery optimization. item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Microsoft Copilot: GPT 6.1 Sol and Claude Sonnet 5.5 beginning to roll out today
item.description:
Updated October 22, 2026: We have updated the content. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and Why:]

To give users more choice and flexibility when working with AI in Microsoft Copilot, we're expanding the set of AI models available in Microsoft Copilot.

Starting today, GPT-6.1 Sol and Claude Sonnet 5.5 begin rolling out with usage-based billing in Cowork and Microsoft Copilot Studio.

GPT-6.1 Sol and Claude Sonnet 5.5 will also begin rolling out in phases across Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Chat in the coming week as part of the Microsoft 365 Copilot user subscription license (USL). Limits apply to these models, but they are designed to support broad day-to-day AI usage across organizations and are implemented in such a way that the vast majority of users are not expected to reach them. Users approaching a limit will receive in-product notifications and can continue their work by switching to Auto mode or selecting another available model. 

[Rollout Schedule:]

  • General Availability:
  • Cowork and Copilot Studio: Rollout begins today, September 30, 2026.
  • Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Chat: Phased rollout begins in the coming week. 

[Impact on Your Organization:

Who is affected:

  • Cowork and Copilot Studio: Users assigned a user subscription license (USL) with usage-based billing (UBB) enabled.
  • Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Chat: Users assigned a user subscription license (USL).
  • Access to Claude Sonnet 5.5 additionally requires the Anthropic subprocessor to be enabled in your organization.
  • Access to GPT-6.1 Sol in select surfaces requires the OpenAI subprocessor to be enabled. Learn more: OpenAI as a subprocessor in Microsoft Online Services | Microsoft Learn. 
  • As a reminder, this setting controls only whether OpenAI models operated by OpenAI (provided by OpenAI as a subprocessor) can be used. OpenAI models operated by Microsoft (Azure OpenAI) aren't affected and remain available in Copilot regardless of this setting.

Platforms/Services:

  • (USL) Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat
  • (USL) Microsoft Word
  • (USL) Microsoft Excel
  • (USL) Microsoft PowerPoint
  • (UBB) Copilot Cowork
  • (UBB) Microsoft Copilot Studio

What will happen:

  • Users will be able to select GPT-6.1 Sol and Claude Sonnet 5.5 using the model selector from supported Microsoft Copilot experiences.
  • The feature is enabled by default for eligible licensed users who meet the applicable configuration requirements.

[Action Required / Recommendations:]

No action is required for organizations that want users to access these models.

Recommended actions:

  • Review whether the Anthropic subprocessor is enabled if you plan to make Claude Sonnet 5.5 available to users.
  • Review whether the OpenAI subprocessor is enabled if you plan to make GPT-6.1 Sol broadly available to users. If disabled, GPT-6.1 Sol may not be available from all supported Copilot surfaces.
  • Review your organization's AI usage guidance and communicate model availability to end users.
  • Inform helpdesk and support teams that users may encounter usage-limit notifications and can continue working using Auto mode or another available model.
  • Review the announcement blog for additional details: Available today: OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Sol and Claude Sonnet 5.5 in Microsoft Copilot | Microsoft Community Hub.
  • Update internal user documentation and training materials, as appropriate.

[Compliance Considerations:]

Consideration Explanation 
Does the change introduce or significantly modify AI/ML or agent capabilities that interact with or provide access to customer data? GPT-6.1 Sol and Claude Sonnet 5.5 are additional AI models that users can select within Microsoft 365 Copilot experiences to generate responses based on content and context available to the user through Copilot. 
Does the change provide end users any new way of interacting with generative AI? Users gain access to new model choices, GPT-6.1 Sol and Claude Sonnet 5.5, in supported Microsoft 365 Copilot experiences. 
Does the change include an admin control and can it be controlled through Entra ID group membership? Access to Claude Sonnet 5.5 depends on administrative configuration of the Anthropic subprocessor.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Viva Engage: Email updates for users without a routable mailbox
item.description:
Updated September 30, 2026: We have updated the content timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[Introduction]

Viva Engage will stop sending email notifications to users who do not have a valid mailbox or routable email destination. Previously, email notifications could still be attempted for these users, resulting in repeated delivery retries, increased load on email systems, and, in some cases, delays to important business communications.

This change reduces unnecessary email traffic, improves delivery efficiency, and helps ensure important communications are delivered reliably and on time.

Users with supported mailbox configurations, including cloud mailboxes, on-premises mailboxes, shared mailboxes, and other routable email destinations, will continue to receive Viva Engage email notifications as expected.

Notifications delivered through supported channels such as Microsoft Teams remain unaffected.

[When this will happen:]

General Availability (Worldwide): Rollout begins mid-October 2026 (previously end of September) and is expected to complete by end of December 2026 (previously end of October).

[How this affects your organization:]

Who is affected:

  • Users who do not have a valid mailbox or routable email destination.
  • Microsoft 365 admins managing Viva Engage users and mailbox configurations.

What will happen:

  • Viva Engage will no longer attempt to send email notifications to users who do not have a valid mailbox or routable email destination.
  • Users with cloud, on-premises, shared, or other supported mailbox configurations will continue to receive email notifications as expected.
  • This change does not affect the existing email notification experience for users with a valid mailbox or routable email destination.
  • Notifications delivered through Microsoft Teams or other supported channels are not impacted.
  • The change is enabled by default and applies automatically.
  • Organizations may see:
    • Reduced load on email systems and gateways.
    • Fewer retry attempts for undeliverable messages.
    • Improved email delivery efficiency and reliability.

[What you can do to prepare:]

  • No action is required.
  • Review your Exchange Online licensing configuration to identify users without mailbox access.
  • Evaluate your notification strategy (e.g., Teams vs. Email) for frontline workers.
  • Inform helpdesk and user support teams of the expected behavior change.
  • Update internal documentation if email notifications are referenced for frontline users.

[Compliance considerations:]

  • Alters how existing customer data is processed: Email notifications to users without mailboxes are no longer attempted, reducing unnecessary processing of undeliverable messages.
  • No other compliance impacts identified.

item.title: [stayInformed] Copilot Code is rolling out in Frontier
item.description:
[What and Why:]

Copilot Code is an AI-powered coding experience in Microsoft Copilot that helps people turn ideas into trackers, dashboards, apps, and other solutions using natural language. Work IQ grounds what they build in emails, meetings, documents, chats, and connected data.

People closest to a problem can build the solution they need while your organization maintains control. Published apps run on Copilot Managed Runtime and inherit your organization’s governance, security, and management controls.

[Rollout Schedule:]

  • Copilot Code: Begins with the Frontier program in late October 2026.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Who is affected:

  • Users in the Frontier program who have a Microsoft 365 Copilot license and are enabled for usage-based billing.
  • Microsoft 365 admins who manage the Copilot app, spending policies, and usage-based billing.

Platforms/Services:

  • Microsoft Copilot app on Windows
  • Microsoft Copilot on the web
  • Microsoft 365 admin center
  • Copilot Managed Runtime
  • Work IQ
  • GitHub, when enabled

What users can do with Copilot Code

  • Users access Code from the Copilot app navigation pane and describe what they want to build. Copilot can ask clarifying questions and use their work context to build the solution.
  • Users can refine what they build through conversation or direct edits. On PC, when local coding is enabled, users can also work with local files and tools or use the terminal.
  • Users can publish projects to Copilot Managed Runtime, a Microsoft-managed cloud environment, and share them with others in their organization. Access to underlying data continues to depend on the user's permissions.
  • Users can connect Code to GitHub when the connection is enabled by an admin.

How admin settings control access

Copilot Code uses usage-based billing. To use Copilot Code, users need:

  • A Microsoft 365 Copilot license.
  • A spending policy.

By default:

  • Cloud coding sessions are enabled on web and PC for eligible users with a Copilot spending policy.
  • Local coding sessions are disabled by default. Admins can allow local coding on PC by setting Code execution location to Cloud and local in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
  • Users covered by a spending policy where the setting "Allow new Agents and services as they become available" is enabled automatically receive access to Code through that spending policy.

For more information about Allow new agents and services setting, see MC1470425.

The following settings determine what users see and can use:

Code spending policyAllow users to discover and use AI experiences enabled by usage-based billingCode execution locationWhat users see
AssignedNo effectCloud (default)Code with cloud coding sessions
AssignedNo effectCloud and localCode with cloud coding sessions and local coding sessions on PC
Not assignedOnNo effectCode entry point and welcome page; Code cannot be used
Not assignedOffNo effectCode entry point is hidden

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

Action is required if you want eligible users to use Copilot Code.

  1. Review the Copilot Code blog.
  2. Deploy the unified Microsoft Copilot app.
  3. For Windows devices participating in Frontier, set the Microsoft Copilot target channel to Beta.
  4. Review your spending policies and confirm that Code is included for the users who should have access. If automatic access to new usage-based services is enabled, review which users will automatically receive Code through their existing spending policy.
  5. Enable Copilot Credit consumption and configure the appropriate spending policies in the Microsoft 365 admin center under Copilot > Cost management.
  6. Decide whether users should have cloud-only coding or cloud and local coding. Local coding is off by default.
  7. Prepare your help desk for the new Code experience, including the in-product experience and your organization's access-request process.
  8. Review information about Copilot Managed Runtime.
  9. Review the Frontier program requirements and guidance.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft Entra: Choose your own telephony provider for SMS and voice authentication
item.description:
[What and why]

Starting October 30, 2026, Microsoft Entra ID will make Choose Your Own Telephony Provider (CYOT) generally available. CYOT enables organizations to use a supported third-party telecommunications provider for SMS and voice authentication. Organizations select a supported provider through Microsoft Security Store and manage their commercial relationship directly with the provider.

Microsoft recommends phishing-resistant authentication methods, such as passkeys, instead of SMS or voice authentication. Organizations should use a telephony provider only for user populations that have a business, regulatory, or technical requirement for telephony-based authentication. 

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning October 30, 2026

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Organizations with users who require SMS or voice authentication for business, regulatory, or technical reasons

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Entra ID
  • Microsoft Security Store

What will happen

  • Starting October 30, 2026, organizations can choose to configure a supported telephony provider for SMS and voice authentication.
  • Your selected provider will deliver the SMS messages or voice calls users need to complete authentication.
  • Microsoft Entra ID will continue to enforce authentication method policies and coordinate the authentication experience.
  • Your organization will manage its commercial relationship with the selected provider.
  • Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication is scheduled to be retired on February 1, 2027, for all users except Global Administrators and external users. The retirement date for Global Administrators and external users is July 1, 2027. Internal guest users remain subject to the February 1, 2027 retirement date.
  • After the applicable retirement date, users whose only available MFA method is SMS or voice must register a passkey during sign-in unless the organization has configured a supported telephony provider. This registration prompt is blocking.

[Action required and recommendations]

If your organization plans to adopt CYOT:

  • Identify affected users. Determine which users have a documented business, regulatory, or technical requirement for SMS or voice authentication.
  • Evaluate phishing-resistant alternatives. Confirm that a phishing-resistant authentication method does not meet the requirements for those users.
  • Review supported telephony providers. Compare providers based on geographic coverage, supported delivery channels, pricing, support, security, and compliance capabilities.
  • Review organizational requirements. Work with the appropriate teams to review procurement, privacy, and regulatory requirements before selecting a provider.
  • Plan your transition. Review Passkeys by default and retirement of Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication and plan your transition based on the retirement date applicable to each user population.
  • Validate purchasing requirements. Review Purchase a SaaS solution and deploy a linked solution. Purchasing through Security Store requires an Azure billing subscription and resource group, plus the appropriate Azure subscription role.
  • Estimate costs. Review provider pricing and expected Azure infrastructure charges before deployment.

Learn more

  • Estimate telephony provider and Azure hosting costs: ExternalPhoneProvider-AzureFunction-Sample/docs/COST-CALCULATOR.md at main · Azure-Samples/ExternalPhoneProvider-AzureFunction-Sample

[Compliance considerations]

item.title: [planForChange] Microsoft Publisher: Reminder that support ends in October 2026

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Migrate Free/Busy, MailTips, and Calendar Sharing before EWS deprecation
item.description:
Updated October 20, 2026: Gov rollout of this feature is paused at this time. We will communicate via Message center when we are ready to proceed. We apologize for any inconvenience.

[What and Why:]

Exchange Web Services (EWS) deprecation begins October 1, 2026. Cross-tenant collaboration features — Free/Busy, MailTips, and Calendar Sharing — currently rely on EWS.

Cross-tenant Free/Busy, MailTips will be available by September 2026 and Calendar Sharing will be available by end-October 2026 via Microsoft 365 Cross-Tenant Access Policy, which replaces EWS-based cross-tenant collaboration.

[Rollout Schedule:]

  • Worldwide: We will begin rolling out in August 2026 and expect to complete by September 15, 2026 for Free/Busy, Mailtips and October 30, 2026 for Calendar Sharing.
  • GCC, GCC High, DoD: We will communicate via Message center when we are ready to proceed.

[Impact on your organization:]

Sharing Free/Busy, Calendars, and MailTips (e.g., out of office message) with another Microsoft 365 organization via Organization Relationship or Sharing Policy relies on Exchange Web Services (EWS), which is being deprecated. To preserve these cross-tenant collaboration scenarios, you will need to start migrating to Microsoft 365 Cross Tenant Access Policy.

Your tenant is affected if it uses any of the following Exchange Online configurations:

  • Organization Relationships — sharing Free/Busy or MailTips with other Microsoft 365 tenants 
  • Sharing Policies — sharing calendars externally, either via invitations sent to recipients in other Microsoft 365 organizations or calendars published for anonymous access via an internet URL

Run these commands in Exchange Online PowerShell to check if your tenant is affected: 

    • Get-OrganizationRelationship | Format-List Name, DomainNames, Enabled, FreeBusyAccessEnabled, FreeBusyAccessLevel, FreeBusyAccessScope, MailTipsAccessEnabled, MailTipsAccessLevel, MailTipsAccessScopeIf results show (1) Enabled: True, and (2) either FreeBusyAccessEnabled: True or MailtipsAccessEnabled: True, and (3) the external organization is hosted in Microsoft 365, your tenant is affected and in scope to migrate. Else, no action is needed. 
    • Get-SharingPolicy | Format-List Name, Domains, Enabled, DefaultIf results show (1) Enabled: True, and (2) the Domains property contains at least one rule with a CalendarSharingFreeBusy access level (Simple, Detail, or Reviewer), and (3) the targeted external organization is hosted in Microsoft 365, and (4) the policy is assigned to one or more mailboxes, your tenant is affected and in scope to migrate. Else, no action is needed.
    • Note: rules that begin with Anonymous: represent calendar publishing to anonymous internet recipients via a published URL - these also appear in this output.

What happens if I do nothing:

Starting October 1, 2026, Exchange Web Services (EWS) will be gradually disabled in line with previous communications linked to this message. As this rollout reaches your tenant, cross-tenant Free/Busy, MailTips, and Calendar Sharing that rely on EWS will be affected — recipients in partner organizations may no longer see Free/Busy, MailTips, or shared calendars from your tenant. 

If your organization is not ready to migrate, you can retain EWS access by following the guidance of the latest blog we published: ExchangeOnline EWS, Your Time is Almost Up (EWSEnabled set to True) while you prepare and execute the migration steps attached to this message. EWS access through this extension will remain available until the final EWS shutdown on April 1, 2027. 

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

  • Follow this Message center post for updates to the rollout schedule. To avoid impact, plan to migrate after the rollout reaches your tenant and before EWS deprecation.
  • Review the migration guide linked below for step-by-step instructions to understand your current configurations, set up new Microsoft 365 Cross Tenant Access Policies, validate the new configurations, and remove unused configurations. 
  • Check the blog post linked below for additional information and answers to frequently asked questions. 
  • Hybrid and on-premises scenarios are not in scope. This update applies to fully cloud-hosted (Exchange Online ↔ Exchange Online) cross-tenant and cross-cloud configurations only. For organizations running on-premises Exchange and Exchange Online in a Hybrid Deployment, migrate to Dedicated Hybrid App. For organizations hosted in Exchange Online sharing with another organization running Exchange on-premises, kindly monitor future Message Center posts for guidance on migration paths as they become available. 

[Additional information:]

item.title: [planForChange] Microsoft Teams: GitHub app consolidation and legacy GitHub app deprecation
item.description:
[What and Why:]

We are consolidating GitHub Notifications and GitHub Copilot capabilities into a single GitHub app in Microsoft Teams. The new app brings repository updates and GitHub Copilot coding capabilities together, so users can follow GitHub activity and act on it within Teams.

As part of this consolidation, the legacy GitHub app will be deprecated by November 16, 2026 and displayed as GitHub (deprecated) until it is retired. Users of the legacy app should remove it from their Teams conversations and add the new app, named GitHub, to those conversations before this date.

Users of the existing GitHub Notifications app need to update the app to the latest version. This app is being renamed GitHub and brings GitHub Copilot capabilities to users with an eligible GitHub Copilot license.

[Rollout Schedule:]

General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in mid-October 2026 and expect to complete by mid-November 2026.

Legacy GitHub app deprecation: The legacy app will be deprecated on November 16, 2026.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

  • Users of the legacy GitHub app: The app will appear as GitHub (deprecated). Users should remove it from their Teams conversations and add the new GitHub app to those conversations before November 16, 2026.
  • Users of GitHub Notifications: The app must be manually updated to the latest version. The app is being renamed GitHub, with GitHub Copilot capabilities available to users with an eligible GitHub Copilot license.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

  • Notify affected users to remove the legacy GitHub app from Teams conversations and add the new GitHub app before November 16, 2026.
  • Review your organization's Teams app access policies to ensure the new GitHub app is available to users who need it.
  • Ask existing users of the GitHub Notifications app to update the app to the latest version.
  • Ask users to confirm that the new GitHub app delivers notifications for the repositories and event types they follow to the intended Teams conversations.
  • If your organization restricts resource-specific consent (RSC), configure the applicable team and chat consent policies to allow the GitHub app’s required RSC permissions so GitHub Copilot can use chat and thread history as context. Learn how to configure RSC permissions here.
  • Update internal guidance to identify the updated app and distinguish it from GitHub (deprecated).

[Compliance considerations:]

Does the change provide a new way of communicating between users, tenants, or subscriptions?No. The change consolidates existing GitHub app capabilities into a single Teams app and deprecates the legacy app.
